chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

The time of Jumuʿah is the sun’s decline, and the time of salat al-ẓuhr during travel is the sun’s decline, and the time of al-ʿaṣr on the day of Jumuʿah in residence is approximately from the time of al-ẓuhr on other than the day of Jumuʿah.

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state affecting the prayer ruling
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةِ: the Friday prayer or the day of Friday in the ruling discussed
key_terms.زَوَالُ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking the start of noon prayer time
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the appointed legal time for an act of worship

ai.seo_question: When does the time of Jumuʿah prayer and Friday ʿAṣr begin according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal timing of salat al-Jumuʿah, salat al-ẓuhr in travel, and salat al-ʿaṣr on Friday for residents. It clarifies that the beginning of these times is linked to zawāl, with Friday carrying a distinct scheduling framework in comparison with other days.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1229 - Al-Halabi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:

"The time for the Jumu’ah prayer (Salat al-Jumu'ah) is at the sun's decline (zawal), and the time for the Dhuhr prayer while traveling is also at the sun's decline. The time for the Asr prayer on Jumu’ah for those who are not traveling is approximately the same as the Dhuhr prayer on other days."
